issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a String (and Part 2 describes the method should return the milk-message String), but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type and Seal/Goat implement it to print the message and return a boolean. The template's Main also expects to print the returned message (treating it as a String). This return-type mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature and prevents them from implementing the expected design (returning the milk message String).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable interface with the problem specification by changing messageOnMilk() to return String (e.g., String messageOnMilk();). Update Seal and Goat to return the milk message String (e.g., return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";) instead of printing and returning a boolean. Ensure code that uses messageOnMilk() (e.g., Main and Farm) treats the return value as a String.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") and describe expected return behavior, but the solution defines the Milkable interface method as returning boolean and the Seal/Goat implementations print the message and return true. This mismatch (String vs boolean) for the same conceptual operation creates a direct naming/type inconsistency and prevents students from mapping the required method signature and behavior in the specification to the solution/template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change the Milkable interface signature to 'String messageOnMilk()' and update Goat and Seal implementations to return the string "[AnimalType] [name] is milked" (e.g., return "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning a boolean. This preserves the intended API and removes the type/signature mismatch.
